_comment: The handoff: the routes the daemon actually loads (engine_seam.ACTIONS_PATHS).
A dialogue page ends in a decision. `approve` closes it and nothing happens
next (config/actions-dialogue.json: task-approved-done). The route here is
the other way to approve: the driver approves what the page decided AND
hands it to a node that carries it out — the `implement` node
(prompts/implement.md). It runs in the same working directory, reads the
approved page as its spec and the driver's closing annotations as the last
instructions before the work starts, does the work, and writes its own
page for the driver to rule on. Same task key, so the fleet shows one
conversation; the reap links the new page derived-from the approved one.
`_label` is what the verdict form shows the driver for this route — the
form line is rendered from it (runnerlib/tasks.route_options), so the words
the driver reads are this file's, not whatever a page author improvised.
Why a route and not a new verdict kind: a route is already the board's word
for 'the driver pointed this somewhere'. The bridge writes `task:route`
with the annotations and the page riding along; this file decides what
that activates. A second destination later is one more action, not code.
config/actions-routes.example.json is a second, unloaded shape (a review
node) kept as documentation; it needs a node nobody has registered.

actions.name: task-approved-handed-to-implement
actions._why: the driver approved the decision on this page and wants it carried out: an implementing agent reads the page as its spec, does the work in the same directory, and writes a page reporting what it did
actions._label: Approve and hand off — an agent carries out what this page decided and brings you a page to review

actions.name: implement-feedback-resumes-implement
actions._why: continue on the implementing agent's page goes back through that agent, resuming its session

payload.note: driver feedback is the next implement turn
